All *Narcissus* species contain the [alkaloid](/wiki/Alkaloid "Alkaloid") poison [lycorine](/wiki/Lycorine "Lycorine"), mostly in the bulb but also in the leaves.[[190]](#cite_note-Pupils_ill_after_bulb_put_in_soup-193) Members of the monocot subfamily [Amaryllidoideae](/wiki/Amaryllidoideae "Amaryllidoideae") present a unique type of alkaloids, the norbelladine alkaloids, which are [4-methylcatechol](/wiki/4-methylcatechol "4-methylcatechol") derivatives combined with [tyrosine](/wiki/Tyrosine "Tyrosine"). They are responsible for the poisonous properties of a number of the species. Over 200 different chemical structures of these compounds are known, of which 79 or more are known from *Narcissus* alone.[[191]](#cite_note-Martin-194)

The toxic effects of ingesting *Narcissus* products for both humans and animals (such as cattle, goats, pigs, and cats) have long been recognised and they have been used in suicide attempts. Ingestion of *N. pseudonarcissus* or *N. jonquilla* is followed by [salivation](/wiki/Salivation "Salivation"), acute abdominal pains, [nausea](/wiki/Nausea "Nausea"), vomiting, and [diarrhea](/wiki/Diarrhea "Diarrhea"), then neurological and cardiac events, including [trembling](/wiki/Trembling "Trembling"), [convulsions](/wiki/Convulsions "Convulsions"), and [paralysis](/wiki/Paralysis "Paralysis"). Death may result if large quantities are consumed.

The toxicity of *Narcissus* varies with species, *N. poeticus* being more toxic than *N. pseudonarcissus*, for instance. The distribution of toxins within the plant also varies, for instance, there is a five times higher concentration of alkaloid in the stem of *[N. papyraceus](/wiki/Narcissus_papyraceus "Narcissus papyraceus")* than in the bulb, making it dangerous to herbivores more likely to consume the stem than the bulb, and is part of the plant's defence mechanisms. In July 1848, Verne left Nantes again for Paris, where his father intended him to finish law studies and take up law as a profession. He obtained permission from his father to rent a furnished apartment at 24 Rue de l'Ancienne-Comédie, which he shared with Édouard Bonamy, another student of Nantes origin.[[27]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELottmann199624-29) (On his 1847 Paris visit, Verne had stayed at 2 Rue Thérèse, the house of his aunt Charuel, on the Butte Saint-Roch.)[[31]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECompère1997c42-33)

Verne arrived in Paris during a time of political upheaval: the [French Revolution of 1848](/wiki/French_Revolution_of_1848 "French Revolution of 1848"). In February, [Louis Philippe I](/wiki/Louis_Philippe_I "Louis Philippe I") had been overthrown and had fled; on 24 February, a provisional government of the [Second Republic](/wiki/Second_French_Republic "Second French Republic") took power, but political demonstrations continued, and social tension remained. In June, barricades went up in Paris, and the government sent [Louis-Eugène Cavaignac](/wiki/Louis-Eug%C3%A8ne_Cavaignac "Louis-Eugène Cavaignac") to crush the insurrection. Verne entered the city shortly before the election of [Louis-Napoléon Bonaparte](/wiki/Napoleon_III "Napoleon III") as the first president of the Republic, a state of affairs that would last until the [coup d'état of 1851](/wiki/1851_French_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat "1851 French coup d'état"). In a letter to his family, Verne described the bombarded state of the city after the recent [June Days uprising](/wiki/June_Days_uprising "June Days uprising") but assured them that the anniversary of [Bastille Day](/wiki/Bastille_Day "Bastille Day") had gone by without any significant conflict.[[32]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJules-Verne197612-34)

Göbekli Tepe :: Construction :: chunk_0009
The plateau Göbekli Tepe is situated on has been shaped by erosion and [quarrying](/wiki/Quarry "Quarry") from the Neolithic onwards. There are four 10-metre-long (33 ft) and 20-centimetre-wide (7.9 in) channels on the southern part of the plateau, interpreted as the remains of an ancient quarry from which rectangular blocks were taken. These are possibly related to a square building in the neighbourhood, of which only the foundation is preserved. Perhaps this is the remains of a Roman [watchtower](/wiki/Watchtower "Watchtower") that was part of the *[Limes Arabicus](/wiki/Limes_Arabicus "Limes Arabicus")*.[[75]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchmidt2006105-75) Most structures on the plateau seem to result from Neolithic quarrying, with the quarries being used as sources for the huge, monolithic architectural elements. Their profiles were pecked into the rock, with the detached blocks, then levered out of the rock bank.[[75]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchmidt2006105-75)

Archaeologists disagree on how much labour was needed to construct the site. Schmidt maintained that "the work of quarrying, transporting, and erecting tons of heavy, monolithic, and almost universally well-prepared limestone pillars [...] was not within the capability of a few people".[[76]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchmidt2006252-76) Using [Thor Heyerdahl](/wiki/Thor_Heyerdahl "Thor Heyerdahl")'s experiments with the [moai](/wiki/Moai "Moai") of [Rapa Nui](/wiki/Rapa_Nui "Rapa Nui") as a reference, he estimated that moving the pillars alone must have involved hundreds of people.[[26]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBanning2011-26) According to these experiments, one *moai* of similar size to a T-shaped pillar from Göbekli Tepe would have taken 20 people a year to carve and 50–75 people a week to transport 15 km.[[77]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDietrichNotroff2015-77) Schmidt's team has also cited a 1917 account of the construction of a megalith on the Indonesian island of [Nias](/wiki/Nias "Nias")

Macau is not a member of the [Community of Portuguese Language Countries](/wiki/Community_of_Portuguese_Language_Countries "Community of Portuguese Language Countries"), despite Portuguese being one of its official languages. This is due to it not being a sovereign nation, but a subnational division of China. In 2006, during the II Ministerial meeting between China and [Portuguese Speaking Countries](/wiki/Community_of_Portuguese_Language_Countries "Community of Portuguese Language Countries"), the CPLP Executive Secretary and Deputy ambassador Tadeu Soares invited the Chief Executive of the Government of the Macau Special Administrative Region, Edmund Ho, to request the Associate Observer status for Macau. The Government of Macau has yet to make this request. In 2016, Murade Murargy, then executive secretary of CPLP said in an interview that Macau's membership is a complicated question, since like the [Galicia region](/wiki/Galicia_(Spain) "Galicia (Spain)") in [Spain](/wiki/Spain "Spain"), it is not an independent country, but only a part of China.[[96]](#cite_note-PontoFinal_2016-10-29-102) However, the *Instituto Internacional de Macau* (澳門國際研究所) and the [University of São José](/wiki/University_of_Saint_Joseph "University of Saint Joseph") are Consultative Observers of the CPLP.[[97]](#cite_note-103)[[98]](#cite_note-104)

The University of Michigan's campus in Ann Arbor is divided into four main areas: the Central Campus area, the North Campus area, the North Medical Campus area, and Ross Athletic Campus area. The campus areas include more than 500 major buildings, with a combined area of more than 37.48 million square feet (860 acres; 3.482 km2). The Central and Athletic Campus areas are contiguous, while the North Campus area is separated from them, primarily by the [Huron River](/wiki/Huron_River_(Michigan) "Huron River (Michigan)"). The North Medical Campus area was developed on Plymouth Road, with several university-owned buildings for outpatient care, diagnostics, and outpatient surgery.[[115]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMacInnes1979-131)
